2.text: and the family would have to apply to a shaman or some other competent

3.text: person to acquire an incantation for future use.

4.text: I have already spoken of the way in which amulets are selected. They

5.text: certainly acquire a great part of their power from incantations pronounced

6.text: over them. The natives explained to me that the ancient charms and

7.text: amulets are very powerful, because of the number of incantations which were

8.text: pronounced over them in a succession of years. Among the Koryak, according

9.text: to Mr. Jochelson, amulets lose power with the lapse of time, and the incan-

10.text: tations must be repeated over them at stated intervals.¹

11.text: Success in the most important pursuits of life is also considered to be

12.text: acquired from incantations, which are pronounced at various times. Thus,

13.text: for instance, success in reindeer-breeding is always ascribed exclusively to

14.text: powerful incantations which belong to the owner, and insure the prosperity

15.text: of his herd. A man well to do must make it his constant care to buy from

16.text: divers people additional incantations good for reindeer-breeding. A poor man,

17.text: on the contrary, is said to be foolish and to have no incantations insuring

18.text: luck in reindeer-breeding. A man whose herd is on the decrease believes

19.text: that his incantations have lost their power, and, if he finally becomes poor,

20.text: he usually throws aside some of his incantations, and loses the remaining

21.text: ones, forgetting the order of the words and actions necessary for their effect.

22.text: The incantation is said to force the owner to lose it.

23.text: In the same way, incantations, among the Maritime people, insure a

24.text: lucky issue in the hunting of sea-mammals. In these the women are considered

25.text: more skilful than the men. Sitting at home, and practising incantations near

26.text: the hearth, they draw the animals toward the shore.² For instance, on a
